structured.approach: I ran DES-01 in check mode, as the brief directs: I checked whether the action is needed and changed nothing. I read both contracted inputs: the approved TRD and the org.architecture feature override. I tested the TRD against the six platform elements that the approved DES-02 design names: topology, runtimes, repository roles, the JSON contract rule, the compatibility rule, and the security, tenancy and storage boundary. I added supporting checks for the data model, the external LLM provider, transport between ap_aging and ap_portal, and the decision log. To ground those checks I read the platform baseline org/org.architecture.md, the feature's org.data_model override and org/org.decision_log.md. I also read the approved feat.design (context_get, revision 722a98f) as background. That design already builds on a "no platform change" position (DD-1, DD-3) and lists the conditions that would reopen it (A8), so this record had to stay consistent with it. An earlier version of the check record existed at the output path. I rewrote it in full from the current inputs, using the K-n IDs and T-n triggers that feat.design cites. A verifier subagent then checked the record against every source. It found four issues: a wrong row range, an overstated match with A8, an inferred claim about PROV-ACME-2026-11, and question IDs that clashed with OQ-1/OQ-2 carried in the TRD. I fixed all four. I used no connector, because the inputs held every fact I needed.

claims.text: DES-01 ran in check mode because the condition 'TRD flags a platform-level change' is not met. No platform architecture document, code, configuration, test or environment was changed.

The TRD touches only ap_pipeline, ap_forecast, ap_aging and ap_portal, the four repositories in one flow that org.architecture already registers. No repository or service is added, and the end-to-end harness is a new test, not a deployed component.
New code keeps to the runtimes org.architecture names, Python 3.9 and Node.js 22 CommonJS. The TRD chooses no new language, framework or library.

The CT-1 contract (ap_aging to ap_portal) carries amount as a two-decimal string and has no date field. This applies the registered rule that JSON between services carries amounts as strings with two decimals and dates as ISO strings; it does not change the rule.

Only two existing functions change, both additively: to_model keeps its signature and return shape, and build_explanation_request gains risk=None as its last parameter. This complies with 'Keep every existing signature; add new functions'.

The TRD adds no storage, schema migration or persistent data, and no change to finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution. The ap_aging baseline rule 'No database, no network, no secrets' still holds.
The feature's registered data model already includes paid_date (date or None), added in feed v3, so no further data-model update is needed.
Provider acme-llm and model acme-text-2 stay unchanged, and vendor_risk uses no LLM. Sending the risk label to the provider is a content question (TQ-8), not a platform change.

The approved design adds no repository, service, runtime, library or storage (DD-1). It adopts CT-1 with an in-library serialiser and no transport layer (DD-3), with TQ-3 still to be confirmed. It states that a new transport would re-trigger DES-01.

The TRD is consistent with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 and D-2026-050. The two conflicts it found in existing code (bucket_for(30), formatAmount) are raised as TQ-1 and TQ-2 and are not changed in this item.

The platform baseline says ap_aging is 'used by the AP API', a component that neither the feature override nor the TRD describes. It is raised as PUQ-2 because it could become a CT-1 transport (trigger T-1).
Conclusion: no platform-level architecture update is needed now. Triggers T-1 to T-7 in the record say what would make the DES-01 action necessary.

open_questions: PUQ-1 (non-blocking, Architect): after release, should the function and invoice-field lists in org/org.architecture.md and the org.architecture override be refreshed with the new functions and the vendor and paid_date keys? This is documentation upkeep, not a platform change.

PUQ-2 (non-blocking, Architect): confirm TQ-3 (who owns CT-1 serialisation and transport) and say what the 'AP API' in the platform baseline is. If it, or any new component, carries CT-1 between ap_aging and ap_portal, trigger T-1 applies and DES-01 must run in full.
structured.summary: I ran DES-01 as a check and wrote the record to outputs/FEAT-ZD-48600/checks/DES-01_feat.platform_update.md. It concludes that no platform architecture update is needed now. The approved TRD stays inside the registered four-repository flow and the Python 3.9 and Node.js 22 runtimes. It keeps every repository's role and applies the JSON contract rule (two-decimal string amounts, ISO dates) without changing it. It follows the rule "keep every existing signature; add new functions", and it adds no storage, network, tenancy, authentication or provider change. These findings match the approved design's DD-1 and DD-3. The record lists the evidence (K-1 to K-10) and seven triggers that would require the action. The main trigger is a transport layer between ap_aging and ap_portal (TQ-3). The record also raises two non-blocking questions for the Architect: whether to refresh the descriptive lists in the platform documents, and what the "AP API" named in the platform baseline is. Nothing was changed. A verifier checked the record against its sources, and all four issues it found are fixed.
